name: Is it worth converting a tub to a shower in a small bathroom?

mainEntity.name: Is it worth converting a tub to a shower in a small bathroom, or does it hurt resale and functionality?
mainEntity.text: Is it worth converting a tub to a shower in a small bathroom, or does it hurt resale and functionality?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tub-to-shower conversion can be a smart upgrade in a small bathroom if the household prefers showers and wants a cleaner, more open layout. It often improves accessibility, makes the room feel less cramped, and allows better use of the available footprint. The tradeoff is that some buyers still want at least one tub in the home, especially families with children. The value of the conversion depends on the rest of the property, how many bathrooms there are, and whether another tub remains elsewhere. In a tight Los Angeles bathroom, the conversion can be especially worthwhile if it replaces an awkward or underused tub with a larger, better-designed shower. Homeowners should think about daily function first and resale second. If the tub is rarely used and the new shower will significantly improve the room, the conversion often makes sense. If the home only has one bathroom and no other tub, keeping a tub may be the safer choice.
acceptedAnswer.description: A tub-to-shower conversion can make a small bathroom feel larger and more usable, especially for daily shower use. It may reduce flexibility for households that need a tub, so the decision depends on lifestyle, future buyers, and whether the layout improves enough to justify the change.
